ruling_text:
Motion to set aside default judgment by defendant Issa Lourdes Marmol. Notice of this continued hearing was provided by the court.

Plaintiff filed this insurance subrogation action against defendant in June 2023, alleging an automobile accident date of June 14, 2022, and an accident location on “Olive Street in the City of San Jose.” (Complaint, ¶¶ 2-6.) A proof of service of summons via substituted service was filed in August 2023. Service was effectuated at an address in Oakland, California. Court default was entered in October 2024. Plaintiff’s declaration in lieu of testimony to support the default judgment does not disclose an accident location. (Stepek dec., filed 10/21/24.) Default judgment was entered against defendant in February 2025 for $17,303.31.
Defendant initially moved ex parte to set aside the default judgment in September 2025. The court denied ex parte relief, but set the matter for a law and motion hearing. The matter was subsequently continued multiple times. A minute order from January 15, 2026 indicates: “the court is perplexed by venue in this case, as it is apparently based on an accident that occurred in Los Angeles County, and defendant has consistently resided in Alameda County- the court would like to hear from the parties about this.”
Code of Civil Procedure section 585.5, subdivision (b) allows a defendant to move to set aside a default judgment and for leave to defend the action in the proper court. The deadline for that motion is 60 days after the defendant first receives notice of levy or notice of any other procedure for enforcing the default judgment. (Ibid.) If the court finds the motion was timely and the action was not commenced in the proper court, the court “shall set aside the default or default judgment on such terms as may be just and shall allow such a party to defend the action in the proper court.” (Id. at subd. (d).) “Unless the plaintiff can show that the plaintiff used reasonable diligence to avoid filing the action in the improper court, upon a finding that the action was commenced in the improper court the court shall award the defendant actual damages and costs, including reasonable attorney’s fees.”
Defendant’s memorandum of points and authorities, filed in September 2025 (though apparently never served on plaintiff), includes attachments. The first appears to be a notice dated August 19, 2025 from the Department of Motor Vehicles that is titled, Order of Suspension. The second is a letter to defendant dated August 26, 2025 from plaintiff’s counsel seeking to collect on the judgment. The third, titled Accident-Incident-Report, summarizes a car accident occurring on “6/14/2022” at “Olive 17th & 18th St” in “LOS ANGELES.” The fourth, titled Los Angeles Police Department Investigative Report, indicates an accident location at “South OLIVE Street/West 17th Street, LOS ANGELES, CA.” Plaintiff’s opposition does not address the venue issue, merely stating the accident occurred “on June 14, 2022, in the city of San Jose.”
Based on the attachments to defendant’s memorandum, the court questions whether venue was appropriate in this case. Defendant appears to reside in Alameda County. And the accident appears to have occurred in Los Angeles County. It appears from the available record that defendant may be entitled to relief under Code of Civil Procedure section 585.5.
Defendant did not cite Code of Civil Procedure section 585.5 in her motion. She also has not complied with Code of Civil Procedure section 585.5, subdivision (c), which requires “an affidavit showing under oath that the action was not commenced in the proper court” as well as “a copy of the answer, motion, or other pleading proposed to be filed in the action.”
The court will continue this matter to allow the parties to brief the Code of Civil Procedure section 585.5 issue. The continued hearing will take place on May 14, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. in Department 10. Defendant’s motion for relief under Code of Civil Procedure section 585.5 must be filed and served no later than April 20, 2026. Plaintiff’s opposition must be filed and served no later than April 30, 2026. Defendant’s reply must be filed and served no later than May 6, 2026. The parties may submit additional documentary evidence about the location of the automobile accident.

expected.case_title: Aspire General Insurance Company v. Issa Lourdes Marmol
